# Lessons ledger

**Read this before starting fleet-wide, credential, or monitoring work.** It is the durable record
of what previous sessions learned the expensive way — findings whose rediscovery costs hours, and
which are not obvious from the code they concern.

This is not a changelog and not a design doc. Every row is something that **surprised somebody**,
with a link to the evidence and a note about which tier is holding it.

## The pattern underneath

Nearly every lesson below is the same shape: **a check exists, and it is not checking.** Dead
trigger, dead credential, swallowed 403, presence-mistaken-for-validity, crashed-suite-looks-green.

The generalization is worth stating on its own, because it predicts new instances:

> **"The check is configured" and "the check works" are different claims, and only the second one
> counts.** Verification means observing the thing do its job — not observing that it is enabled.

A corollary that has caught real defects: **a monitor's first report is not evidence the monitor
works.** When a new checker's debut finding is "several things are broken," verify against an
independent signal before anyone acts on it (L03).

## How a tier is chosen

| Tier                     | When                                                          |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **CI test / hook**       | the lesson is mechanically detectable in the tree             |
| **Workflow guard**       | the lesson is about runtime behavior a workflow can assert    |
| **`doc —` (prose only)** | genuine judgement, or an external fact no local check can see |

Push each lesson to the **strongest tier that can hold it**. A `doc —` cell must say _why_ prose is
the ceiling; "nobody got round to it" is a gap, and gaps get a linked follow-up issue rather than a
silent prose entry.

## Adding a lesson

Append a row to the matching table. `tests/workflow-logic/test_lessons_ledger.py` enforces the
contract, so a malformed or unenforceable row fails CI:

- **ID** — `L##`, unique, never renumbered **once merged** (merged IDs are cited from issues and
  PRs). An ID in an open PR is only a _reservation_: concurrent drafts routinely pick the same next
  number, and whichever merges first owns it. Before promoting a ledger PR, re-check `main`'s
  highest ID and renumber your own rows if they collide — then assert `uniq -d` over the IDs,
  because a merge that resolves the table cleanly can still leave a duplicate (L43).
- **Lesson** — the transferable claim, not the incident. "Presence ≠ validity" travels; "repo X had
  a stale lockfile on the 24th" does not.
- **Evidence** — an issue/PR/run reference (`#123`) or a URL. A lesson with no evidence link is a
  rumour.
- **Enforced by** — backticked repo path(s) that hold the lesson, **or** `doc — <reason>`. Paths are
  checked for existence: a ledger that claims enforcement which is not there would be this
  document's own failure mode, one level up.

Add the row in the **same PR as the fix**, while the surprise is still fresh.

An ID that is skipped on `main` must be **declared** in the block below, with the PR holding it. A
gap that is not declared is not a reservation — it is a row that fell out of a merge, which is what
happened to L38 (restored from `7b3733d` in #1113 after `28a4b8b` dropped it while re-padding the
whole table). `tests/workflow-logic/test_lessons_ledger.py` fails on any undeclared gap.

**Every entry you add below is a merge-order coupling to the PR named in it, and composing against
`main` will not show it to you.** The guard fails an entry whose id has since become a row — L181,
deliberately, so the block cannot silt up into the blanket waiver it replaced. That is not the trap.
The trap is that the entry is written while its holder is still open, so your branch and the
holder's touch different lines: git merges them cleanly, both PRs read green against `main`, and
only their union is red. L191 is this failure with the holder already landed, and AGENTS.md's
composition recipe catches that one. **It does not catch the sibling case** — measured 2026-08-23 on
#1214 (declaring `L248 #1209`, `L249 #1209`, `L250 #1212`) against #1212 (landing all three as
rows): each composes green against `main`, and their union fails this guard in either landing order.
So compose against the **holder's head**, which the entry names for you, and not only against
`main`:

```bash
git fetch origin <holder-branch>
WT=$(mktemp -d); git worktree add -q "$WT" --detach origin/main && cd "$WT"
git merge --no-edit <your-head> && git merge --no-edit FETCH_HEAD
python3 tests/workflow-logic/test_lessons_ledger.py; echo "exit=$?"
```

Resolution when it is red: whoever reaches the queue second deletes the matching lines from the
block — verified to be the whole fix on that pair, 48 PASS / rc=0, nothing else in the merge
touched.

Because a finding fails the run and 740 watches 745, the steady state is a rolling alert issue reopening most mornings — the alert fatigue the silent-when-clean pattern exists to prevent, arriving through the definition rather than the pattern. Once the platform is serving again the same run does **not** recover: it stays parked, and _then_ close and reopen is right, which is why the mode question must be re-asked rather than answered once. Ask for the jobs count before choosing a remedy; it is one call and it is the only thing that separates the two.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | run 110 diagnosis of #1093 and #1062, confirmed run 111: after Actions recovered, `31118667543` was still `queued`/0 jobs, and close plus reopen moved #1093 from `blocked` to `CLEAN` on the **same** sha `2f7a96a` with no new commit                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | doc — pending #1028, which owns the mechanical half; Both halves were false and both were falsifiable at the time. (a) The delivery it was written about had **already merged 3m46s before that comment was posted**, by `github-actions[bot]` via the TARGET repo's own `reconcile-data-prs.yml` — an automated merge path that had been ticking every 30 minutes for weeks and was never looked for, because the agent's inability had been silently promoted into the system's. (b) The refusal was **transient**: the identical call armed auto-merge on #1176 first try one run later and it merged. What makes this a row rather than a bug report is that run 145 _observed_ the transience and reasoned past it — it recorded that `gh project item-add` was blocked intermittently and succeeded on retry, then used that contrast to argue the merge block was permanent (_"the merge calls never succeeded"_), where the evidence only supported _"did not succeed in the attempts one run made"_. The failure is not pessimism; it is scope. **From a refusal, conclude that this call failed now. Before concluding a capability is gone, look for the path that does not run through you** — here the system had one and it was already working. The mechanical half — that a data delivery has an automated merge path with three conditions — is documentation and is filed as #1177 |

Two conductor runs hand-wrote standalone probes rather than fix it, because on the platform CI uses there was nothing to see. Enforce that class **statically, against the source**, where it is visible from every host. The same asymmetry hides the fix's own regressions: on POSIX `os.pathsep` is `:`, so a hardcoded `:` satisfies every runtime assertion while reintroducing the bug on Windows — that one had to be pinned by reading the source. This is not test-only — `scripts/generate-agentic-os-status.py`, which produces the **public** status feed, dies with `UnicodeEncodeError` on the 🚨 in #921's title unless `PYTHONUTF8=1` is set. It is not correct; it is constant. Minimal repro on this host (GNU grep 3.0 under git-bash), against a 3-line CRLF file and a 3-line LF file each written byte-exactly from Python: direct probe on the CRLF file -> **0** (rc 1, wrong); direct on the LF file -> 0 (rc 1, right); the same call inside `$( )` on the CRLF file -> **3** (right by accident); inside `$( )` on the LF file -> **3** (wrong — the L175 case).
